newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends lower as crop concerns diminish.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends lower as crop concerns diminish.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed lower on diminished concerns about widespread yield losses this week in the northern portion of the U.S. corn growing region, traders said.
"Some of the midday's (weather forecasts) moved the frost line further north and had a little warmer temperatures," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co.
Corn was boosted early on forecasts for freezing weather this week in portions of the Midwest corn growing region, traders said.
Agronomists Wednesday said frost damage should be light.
"Your absolute yield loss is not going to be all that great," said Don White, University of Illinois agronomist.
Corn rallied early on the freeze talk and on a technical bounce, the traders said.

"The market is very short, it's way oversold but the weather is the main game," said Paul Haugens, vice president for FIMAT Futures. The nine day relative strength index (RSI) for December closed Wednesday at 14.271. Oversold is generally considered to be 20 or less.
Corn closed 1/2 to 3-1/4 cents per bushel lower, with December down 3-1/4 at $2.92-3/4.
Corn futures volume was estimated at 80,000 contracts, down from 89,757 Tuesday, according to the CBOT.
Corn options volume was estimated at 37,000 contracts, down from 48,332 Tuesday.
